## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The dream of the king  (`#the-dream-of-the-king`)

Cited ayat: 12:43-49

> **12:43** وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِى فِى رُءْيَٰىَ إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ
>
> **12:44** قَالُوٓا۟ أَضْغَٰثُ أَحْلَٰمٍ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحْلَٰمِ بِعَٰلِمِينَ
>
> **12:45** وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا۠ أُنَبِّئُكُم بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦ فَأَرْسِلُونِ
>
> **12:46** يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِى سَبْعِ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ لَّعَلِّىٓ أَرْجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
>
> **12:47** قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًا فَمَا حَصَدتُّمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ
>
> **12:48** ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ سَبْعٌ شِدَادٌ يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ
>
> **12:49** ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ عَامٌ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (12:43): The king said that he saw seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain and other dry ones; he asked his chiefs to explain his vision if they could interpret visions.

**c2** (12:44): They said that it was a confusion of dreams and that they had no knowledge of the interpretation of such dreams.

**c3** (12:45): The one who had been saved remembered after a period, said that he would inform them of its interpretation and asked to be sent.

**c4** (12:46): He came to Yusuf, addressed him as the truthful one, and asked for the interpretation of the cows and the ears, so that he might return to the people and they might know.

**c5** (12:47): Yusuf said that they would sow for seven years continuously, and that what they harvested they should leave in its ear, except a little for eating.

**c6** (12:48): Yusuf said that after that would come seven hard years that would eat what they had stored for them, except a little of what they preserved.

**c7** (12:49): Yusuf said that after that would come a year in which people would be given relief and in which they would press.

### One-minute summary

The king saw seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones and seven green ears and seven dry ones, and his chiefs could not interpret it [c1][c2]. The man who had been saved came to Yusuf, and Yusuf gave the interpretation of seven years, then seven hard years, then a year of relief [c4][c5][c6][c7].

### Complete story

The king said that he saw seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain and other dry ones, and asked his chiefs to explain his vision if they could interpret visions [c1]. They said that it was a confusion of dreams and that they had no knowledge of the interpretation of such dreams [c2].

The one who had been saved remembered after a period, said that he would inform them of its interpretation and asked to be sent [c3]. He came to Yusuf, addressed him as the truthful one, and asked for the interpretation, so that he might return to the people and they might know [c4].

Yusuf said that they would sow for seven years continuously, and that what they harvested they should leave in its ear, except a little for eating [c5]. After that would come seven hard years that would eat what they had stored, except a little of what they preserved [c6]. After that would come a year in which people would be given relief and in which they would press [c7].

### Deep study

The vision is given once and the interpretation follows it in steps [c1][c5][c6][c7]. The chiefs decline [c2], and the man who had been saved is the link to Yusuf [c3][c4]. The Arabic for what the people would press does not say what was pressed [c7].

### Kids mode

The king dreamed of seven fat cows eaten by seven thin ones [c1]. Yusuf said there would be seven years of sowing, then seven hard years, then a year of relief [c5][c6][c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the interpretation comes with instructions to keep a store through the years of plenty [c5][c6]. Another is that the one who forgot Yusuf earlier remembers him when the chiefs cannot answer [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- The Quran does not name the king or the land he ruled; it uses the word king for the ruler in this account. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: names for the king, his dynasty and his title; none is used here.
- Not established: who the chiefs were or how long the period of 12:45 was.
- The Arabic for press does not say what was pressed (grapes, olives or something else).
- Not established: how long after the prison scene this came.

## 2. From prison to authority  (`#from-prison-to-authority`)

Cited ayat: 12:50-57

> **12:50** وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱئْتُونِى بِهِۦ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُ ٱلرَّسُولُ قَالَ ٱرْجِعْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَسْـَٔلْهُ مَا بَالُ ٱلنِّسْوَةِ ٱلَّٰتِى قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ إِنَّ رَبِّى بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِيمٌ
>
> **12:51** قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ رَٰوَدتُّنَّ يُوسُفَ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ قُلْنَ حَٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِن سُوٓءٍ قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْـَٰٔنَ حَصْحَصَ ٱلْحَقُّ أَنَا۠ رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
>
> **12:52** ذَٰلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّى لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى كَيْدَ ٱلْخَآئِنِينَ
>
> **12:53** وَمَآ أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِىٓ إِنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌۢ بِٱلسُّوٓءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّىٓ إِنَّ رَبِّى غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
>
> **12:54** وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱئْتُونِى بِهِۦٓ أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِى فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُۥ قَالَ إِنَّكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ
>
> **12:55** قَالَ ٱجْعَلْنِى عَلَىٰ خَزَآئِنِ ٱلْأَرْضِ إِنِّى حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ
>
> **12:56** وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَآءُ نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَن نَّشَآءُ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
>
> **12:57** وَلَأَجْرُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ يَتَّقُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (12:50): The king ordered that Yusuf be brought to him; when the messenger came, Yusuf told him to return to his lord and ask about the women who had cut their hands, for his Lord knows their plotting.

**c2** (12:51): The king asked the women what their affair was when they tried to seduce Yusuf; they said that they knew no evil against him; and the wife of the Aziz said that now the truth had become clear: she had tried to seduce him and he was among the truthful.

**c3** (12:52-53): A speaker, not named in the verses, says that this was so that the master would know that he had not betrayed him in his absence, and that God does not guide the plotting of the betrayers; and that he does not declare himself innocent, for the self commands evil except where his Lord has mercy.

**c4** (12:54): The king said to bring Yusuf to him, that he would take him for himself; and when he had spoken with him, the king said that he was that day established with them and trusted.

**c5** (12:55): Yusuf asked to be set over the storehouses of the land, saying that he was a knowing guardian.

**c6** (12:56): God says that in this way He established Yusuf in the land, where he could settle wherever he wished; He reaches with His mercy whomever He wills and does not waste the reward of those who do good.

**c7** (12:57): The reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and are mindful of God.

### One-minute summary

The king sent for Yusuf, and Yusuf asked him to look into the matter of the women who had cut their hands [c1]. The women and the wife of the Aziz spoke, and the king then gave Yusuf his trust, and Yusuf asked to be set over the storehouses of the land [c2][c4][c5].

### Complete story

The king ordered that Yusuf be brought to him; when the messenger came, Yusuf told him to return to his lord and ask about the women who had cut their hands [c1]. The king asked the women what their affair was; they said that they knew no evil against him, and the wife of the Aziz said that now the truth had become clear: she had tried to seduce him and he was among the truthful [c2].

A speaker, not named in the verses, says that this was so that the master would know that he had not betrayed him in his absence, and that he does not declare himself innocent, for the self commands evil except where his Lord has mercy [c3].

The king said to bring Yusuf to him, and when he had spoken with him, said that he was that day established with them and trusted [c4]. Yusuf asked to be set over the storehouses of the land, saying he was a knowing guardian [c5]. God says that in this way He established Yusuf in the land [c6], and that the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and are mindful of God [c7].

### Deep study

The chapter has the investigation of the women [c1][c2], a speech whose speaker the verses do not name [c3], the king's trust [c4], Yusuf's request [c5] and God's comment on it [c6][c7]. The draft does not decide who speaks 12:52-53 and says so [c3]. The Quran does not narrate the moment of Yusuf's release from prison [c1].

### Kids mode

The king sent for Yusuf, and the women said they knew no evil against him [c1][c2]. The king trusted him, and Yusuf asked to be set over the storehouses of the land [c4][c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Yusuf asks that the matter of the women be cleared before he comes out [c1][c2]. Another is that the passage ends by saying the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and are mindful of God [c7].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how long after the king's dream these events came, or the title and rank of the post Yusuf asked for; the verse says the storehouses of the land.
- The verses do not say who speaks 12:52-53. Some read it as Yusuf and some as the wife of the Aziz; a reviewer must confirm, because the verses do not name the speaker.
- The Quran does not narrate the moment of Yusuf's release; he says later (12:100) that God brought him out of the prison, which is outside this record.
- The Quran does not say in so many words that the king granted the post; 12:56 says God established Yusuf in the land.
